title: Cost-efficient tier: aggressive batching + throughput tuning with queue blow-up guardrails
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Goal
- Tune the cost-efficient SLO tier to improve throughput and $/1K tokens via more aggressive continuous batching, while preventing tail-latency/queue collapse under bursty concurrency.
- This ticket focuses specifically on the scheduler knobs + safety mechanisms for the cost-efficient tier. Tier selection plumbing + telemetry reason codes are tracked separately.

Context
- Cost-efficient tier is intended for non-interactive / background workloads (summarization, indexing, offline runs) where customers trade latency for unit economics.
- Risk: pushing batch sizes / wait budgets too far can create queue blowups (head-of-line blocking, pathological backlog growth) and starvation for long-prefill requests.

Non-goals
- Per-tenant real-time auto-tuning. We ship defaults + heuristics based on workload signals.
- Any change to routing across regions/capacity tiers.

Proposed changes (cost-efficient tier)
1) More aggressive batching (decode-focused)
- Increase max_batch_tokens and max_wait_ms in cost-efficient tier relative to standard.
- Allow larger decode batches when queue is stable, but cap prefill batch to avoid long-pause prefill stalls.
- Prefer continuous batching that opportunistically merges decode steps while keeping per-request fairness.

2) Max token batching limits (hard caps + dynamic caps)
- Introduce a hard cap for cost-efficient tier batch_tokens by model-family + hardware class (initially: top 2 model families on H100/A100; expand later).
- Add a dynamic cap based on current queue depth and prefill/decode ratio:
  - When queue_depth_requests or queue_depth_tokens exceeds threshold, reduce target batch_tokens and wait budget to stop positive feedback loops.
  - When prefill_fraction is high (many long prompts), lower batch_tokens ceiling to prevent prefill from monopolizing the step budget.

3) Safeguards against queue blowups
- Backpressure / admission control for cost-efficient tier only:
  - If queue_depth_tokens > Q_MAX_TOKENS or estimated_queue_delay_ms > Q_MAX_DELAY_MS, start shedding new requests with a tier-specific overload response (429/503 depending on caller policy), emitting reason code: overload_mode.
  - Add hysteresis so we don’t flap in/out of overload mode.
- Starvation prevention:
  - Ensure long-prefill requests are not perpetually deferred behind many short decodes.
  - Add fairness window: every N scheduler ticks, reserve capacity for oldest request cohort (age-based).
- Queue instrumentation:
  - Emit queue_depth_tokens, queue_depth_requests, estimated_queue_delay_ms with tier label (cardinality controlled elsewhere).

Implementation notes
- Scheduler knobs live behind the tier profile config. For this ticket we wire cost-efficient defaults + guardrails into the scheduler policy layer:
  - target_batch_tokens_cost_efficient
  - max_batch_tokens_cost_efficient (hard)
  - max_wait_ms_cost_efficient
  - prefill_batch_token_cap_cost_efficient
  - overload_queue_delay_ms_cost_efficient
  - overload_queue_tokens_cost_efficient
  - overload_hysteresis_ms
- Guardrails must be enforced before request enqueue growth becomes unbounded (i.e., decision must be based on projected queue delay, not just current).

Acceptance criteria
Perf / economics
- On benchmark-lab mixed workload suite (ENG-18427 scenarios), cost-efficient tier shows:
  - Throughput improvement vs standard tier: +15% tokens/sec (target; note: per-model will vary)
  - $/1K tokens improvement: measurable decrease attributable to higher effective batch utilization (target: 8–12% depending on model)
- No regressions in correctness (golden outputs within expected nondeterminism) and no increase in truncation / streaming chunk anomalies.

Stability / safety
- Under burst test (concurrency ramp + long-prompt injection):
  - Queue does not diverge (queue_depth_tokens stabilizes or triggers overload mode within thresholds)
  - Overload mode triggers with clear telemetry and does not flap more than once per hysteresis window
  - No starvation: max request age bounded (define bound in benchmark pass/fail gate; initial: <= 4x median age at steady state)

Observability
- Reason codes emitted when overload guardrails engage (requires ENG-18426): overload_mode, dynamic_cap_applied.
- Dashboard panels can slice queue depth and batch tokens by tier.

Rollout
- Feature flagged; can be enabled for internal canary + small hosted subset.
- Clear rollback: revert cost-efficient tier to standard-like knobs via config without code revert.

Links / related work
- GitHub: PR-28466 cost-efficient tier aggressive batching + guardrails (owner: Omar). (In review)
- GitHub: benchmark-lab PR-612 mixed-workload tier scenarios (needed for final verification).
- Slack: eng-runtime thread on overload behavior per tier (reference for hysteresis thresholds).

Open questions
- Do we allow cost-efficient tier to increase max_wait_ms for streaming endpoints if customer misconfigures? Current proposal: if streaming=true, clamp cost-efficient wait budget to standard-tier max_wait_ms and emit reason code: streaming_clamp.
- Do we return 429 vs 503 in overload mode? Current proposal: default 429 for hosted API; Dedicated clusters can map to 503 based on tenant policy.

Activity / updates
- 2026-01-22 (Omar): Initial knob sweep on H100 (Llama-family) shows best tokens/sec at +35% batch_tokens, but queue_delay spikes >3x under burst. Adding queue-delay-based dynamic cap stabilizes without losing most gains.
- 2026-02-03 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure overload triggers are tier-scoped; don’t trip global admission for fast/standard.
- 2026-02-10 (Claire Dubois): Add a long-prompt-heavy scenario to catch prefill monopolization. Marcus is adding to perf suite; we should gate cost-efficient profile there too.
- 2026-02-18 (Allison Grant): Telemetry must avoid high-cardinality tags. Tier label ok; do NOT tag with raw batch_tokens. Bucket if needed.
- 2026-02-24 (Omar): Implemented hysteresis + age-based fairness window. Waiting on perf suite run; early local run shows no starvation with N=32 ticks.
- 2026-02-27 (Sofia): Marking In Review pending benchmark-lab CI results + perf canary dry-run. If numbers hold, we’ll merge behind feature flag for internal canary next.

Reviewer checklist
- Confirm dynamic cap logic cannot oscillate every tick (hysteresis + smoothing)
- Confirm overload mode is per-tier and does not interfere with standard/fast routing
- Confirm guardrail thresholds are configurable per model family/hardware
- Confirm metrics include tier + model_family but not tenant_id / route_id by default

Notes for release (runtime-1.22)
- Cost-efficient tier may shed load earlier than standard tier under sustained overload to avoid runaway queue growth.
- For streaming endpoints, cost-efficient tier is clamped to preserve chunk latency stability (if enabled, customers should opt into standard/fast).
